clue.text: Cord with bits pulled back

indicators.note: something pulled back is drawn the other way, so the word is read from its end to its start

blocks.note: bits and pieces are parts

explanation.surface: A length of cord with frayed bits drawn back along it.
explanation.definitionFit: A strap is a strip of leather or fabric used for fastening, close kin to a binding cord.

clue.text: Where brew served up to me, or a fancy

indicators.note: a fancy version is an elaborate reworking, so the letters before it are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters of these three short words

explanation.surface: Someone offered tea asks where it is served, then says it's up to them, or a fancy place.
explanation.walkthrough: A brew is British slang for a cup of tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A tearoom is a small café or restaurant whose business is serving pots of tea and cakes.

clue.text: Where shelf stackers may be seen, everywhere

definitions.text: Where shelf stackers may be seen

blocks.clueFragment: Where shelf stackers may be seen
blocks.note: first meaning, taken literally: staff who restock shelves work throughout a store
second meaning: an informal British phrase for scattered or in disarray in every direction

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is British slang for scattered or disorganised; the first half reads it literally as being all over a shop floor.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes things strewn in every direction, so it stands for spread about in all places.

clue.text: Early spring parade

blocks.note: first meaning: the month that opens the season in the northern hemisphere
second meaning: a procession of people walking in step

explanation.surface: A procession held in the first days of the season.
explanation.definitionFit: The third month falls at the start of spring, and as a noun the word also means a formal procession on foot.

clue.text: Month before it turns up south of an island

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means reading from bottom to top, the opposite way
in a down entry, being south of something means sitting below it, so that part follows

blocks.note: taken as written
AUG is the calendar abbreviation for August
taken as written

explanation.surface: A traveller notes that the month before the holiday turns up, heading south of an island.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'south of' means the later piece is written below, so it follows in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Antigua is a Caribbean island, part of the nation of Antigua and Barbuda.

clue.text: Tailor shortened tux carried by messenger

indicators.note: something shortened has had its end cut off, so the last letter goes
what is carried is held inside the carrier, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: a courier delivers messages and parcels
taken as written, before its last letter is removed

explanation.surface: A tailor sends a trimmed dinner jacket across town with a courier.
explanation.walkthrough: Tux is short for tuxedo, the American name for a dinner jacket.
explanation.definitionFit: A couturier is a designer and maker of fashionable clothes, a high-end tailor or dressmaker.

clue.text: Lack of American sense

blocks.note: no as in 'no money', a lack of it
US abbreviates United States

explanation.surface: A jibe that Americans lack common sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Nous is British informal for practical intelligence, common sense or gumption.

clue.text: An egg that’s scrambled kept by Victor and girl in vessel

indicators.note: scrambled eggs are stirred up, so the letters are mixed into a new order
what is kept by someone is held within their grasp, so it goes inside

blocks.note: a victor is a champion, CHAMP for short
the letters of these two words
lass is a northern British word for a girl

explanation.surface: A cook's mishap: a scrambled egg ends up held by a winner and his girlfriend in a bowl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' suggests a ship, but a drinking glass is a vessel too.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall flute or wide coupe for fizzy wine is a drinking vessel in the broad sense.

clue.text: Fair promise broken by Liberal, scuffle finally ensuing

indicators.note: a word broken by another is split open with that other placed in the gap
finally points to the end, so only the last letter is kept
ensuing means following on, so this piece comes after the rest

blocks.note: a bond is a binding promise
L is the standard abbreviation for Liberal
the final letter of this word

explanation.surface: A fair promise is broken by a Liberal politician, and a scuffle follows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fair' looks like a judgement on the promise but is the definition, for light hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair hair is light-coloured, the same shade described as blonde, especially of a woman.

clue.text: Evening wear exactly right, laic surprisingly impressed

indicators.note: a surprising outcome is an unexpected arrangement, so these letters are reordered
impressed means pressed into, so this piece is pushed inside the other

blocks.note: 'to a T' means precisely, exactly right
taken as written

explanation.surface: A lay person is pleasantly surprised that their evening outfit fits exactly right.
explanation.walkthrough: Laic means lay, not clerical; it is the anagram fodder, not part of the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A tailcoat is a formal jacket cut away at the front, worn with white tie in the evening.

clue.text: Wicked without gaps, did you say?

indicators.note: asking what someone said points to the sound of the words rather than their spelling

blocks.note: something with no holes could jokingly be called un-holey

explanation.surface: Someone queries whether a seamless thing is wicked.
explanation.walkthrough: The invented word for having no holes is pronounced the same as the word for sinful.
explanation.definitionFit: Unholy means sinful or ungodly, so it stands in for evil or wicked.

clue.text: Scrabble vowels for team

indicators.note: to scrabble is to scramble about, and the board game shuffles letter tiles too

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A Scrabble player needs vowels to make up a team of tiles.
explanation.walkthrough: Wolves is the nickname of Wolverhampton Wanderers, an English football club.
explanation.definitionFit: The football club from Wolverhampton is universally known by this nickname, so it names a sports side.

clue.text: Bloke into fruit, foodie

indicators.note: going into something means entering it, so this piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: a gourd is a hard-skinned fruit such as a squash
a bloke is a man in British slang

explanation.surface: A man who is really into fruit is a foodie.
explanation.definitionFit: A gourmand loves eating and good cooking, much as a modern food enthusiast does.

clue.text: Sadly, animal knocked over wine

indicators.note: something knocked over is upended, so the letters run the other way

blocks.note: alas is a cry of sorrow
a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: An animal clumsily tips a glass of wine over.
explanation.definitionFit: Marsala is a fortified wine from Sicily, used in cooking and as a dessert drink.

clue.text: Emergent, a new deal

indicators.note: a new version of these letters is a fresh arrangement of them

blocks.note: the letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A new deal is emerging from negotiations.
explanation.definitionFit: A deal between parties is an arrangement or pact they have settled on together.

clue.text: Game is broadcast in pictures

indicators.note: broadcast seed is scattered widely, so the letters are scattered into a new order

blocks.note: the letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A match is shown on television in moving pictures.
explanation.definitionFit: Images are visual representations such as photographs or drawings, so they are pictures.

clue.text: Legendary monarch, king in a day

indicators.note: being in something means sitting within it, so this letter goes inside

blocks.note: A plus THUR, a short form of Thursday
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A famous king of legend who was monarch only for a day.
explanation.definitionFit: King Arthur of Camelot and the Round Table is the best-known ruler of British legend.

clue.text: Premier League team, neither top nor bottom, fine

indicators.note: in a down entry the top and bottom are the first and last letters, and both are removed

blocks.note: Brighton and Hove Albion play in England's top football division

explanation.surface: A football club sitting mid-table in the Premier League is doing fine.
explanation.walkthrough: Brighton is a seaside city on England's south coast whose football club is in the Premier League.
explanation.definitionFit: Righto is a chirpy British way of saying OK or all right, agreeing that something is fine.

clue.text: Vegetable, standard crop

blocks.note: par is the standard or normal level
to crop or cut is to snip

explanation.surface: A vegetable grown as a standard crop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crop' suggests a harvest but means a cut.
explanation.definitionFit: The parsnip is a pale root vegetable related to the carrot, an example of the category.

clue.text: Beer bottles finished off, German exercises

indicators.note: to bottle something is to enclose it, so this word goes around the next

blocks.note: Pils is a pale lager, short for Pilsner
having finished off a meal, one ate it

explanation.surface: Beer bottles are emptied before a German workout.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition's German refers to Joseph Pilates, the German who devised the system.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilates is a regime of controlled core-strengthening moves devised by a German trainer, Joseph Pilates.

clue.text: Good one, sovereign trailblazer

blocks.note: PI is short for pious, so good
taken as written
ER is the royal cipher of Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A good monarch who blazes a trail.
explanation.definitionFit: A pioneer is the first to explore or develop something, opening the way for followers.

clue.text: Clutch very bad, fragile thing

blocks.note: a clutch is a set of eggs laid together
something hellish is very bad

explanation.surface: A clutch that went very badly wrong, and something fragile broken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clutch' suggests grabbing or a car pedal; here it is a nest of eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: The outer casing of an egg is famously thin and breakable, the proverbial delicate object.

clue.text: Thug from Los Angeles in pool

indicators.note: a person from a city carries its name before them, so the place comes first

blocks.note: LA abbreviates Los Angeles
a goon is a hired heavy

explanation.surface: A Los Angeles thug turns up in a swimming pool.
explanation.definitionFit: A lagoon is a stretch of shallow water cut off from the sea, a natural pool.

clue.text: Upward spin for eye

indicators.note: in a down entry, going upward means reading from the bottom, so the word runs backwards

blocks.note: to reel is to whirl or spin round

explanation.surface: An upward spin of the ball catches the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: To leer is to look at someone in a lascivious way, so it is a way to eye them.

clue.text: In a mo, the dancing

indicators.note: dancing letters move about and settle into a new order

blocks.note: the letters of these three words; mo is British for a moment

explanation.surface: In a moment, the dancing starts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a preposition starting the phrase, but it is the definition, as in 'staying in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is in has stayed in their own house rather than going out.

clue.text: Youth in great need, virtually abandoned

indicators.note: virtually means almost, so the word stops just short of its last letter
abandoned means wild and uninhibited, so the letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, before its last letter goes

explanation.surface: A young person in great need, practically left to fend for themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: A youth is a young person, and someone aged thirteen to nineteen is exactly that.

clue.text: Hidden supply stolen by larcenist, a shame

indicators.note: what is stolen by these words is held within them, tucked inside the letters

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word into the next two

explanation.surface: A secret hoard was taken by a thief, which is a shame.
explanation.definitionFit: A stash is a secret store of something, such as money or provisions put away out of sight.

clue.text: Seize unlicensed stock, unloading remaining packages first of all

indicators.note: first of all asks for the first letter of every one of the preceding words

blocks.note: the opening letter of each of these five words

explanation.surface: Seize unlicensed goods, unloading the remaining packages first.
explanation.definitionFit: To usurp is to take a position or power by force, wrongly grabbing it.
